cards.text: The Teacher, son of David and king in Jerusalem, is writing down what he sees under the sun (Ecclesiastes 1:1). He just said there's a time for everything, and that God will call to account what has passed (Ecclesiastes 3:1, 3:15). Now he looks at the place of judgment and the place of righteousness, the spots where things are supposed to be set right.

cards.question: In the place of judgment and the place of righteousness, what does the Teacher find?

cards.text: That's like calling the fire department and finding out the fire department is the thing on fire. So the Teacher says something in his heart about God.

cards.question: The Teacher says in his heart that God will judge both the righteous and the wicked.
God will judge them, the Teacher says, since there is a ___ for every activity and every deed.

cards.text: Then the Teacher says something to himself about the sons of men. God tests them, he says, so they can see for themselves what they really are.

cards.question: What does the Teacher say God's test shows the sons of men they are?

cards.text: OUCH. Friend, I'm a cookie stamper with a mustache for hands, and even I felt that one. Then the Teacher looks at how men and animals die.

cards.question: How does the Teacher say men and beasts compare when they die?
The Teacher says men and beasts each have a different breath.

cards.text: Man has no advantage over the animals, the Teacher says, since everything is futile. I spent YEARS in a junk drawer feeling fancier than the rubber bands in there with me, and friend, we were in the SAME drawer.

cards.question: All go to one place: all come from dust, and all return to ___.

cards.text: Then the Teacher brings up the spirit of man rising upward and the spirit of the animal going down into the earth.

cards.question: The Teacher says he knows for sure that the spirit of man rises upward.

cards.text: He's looked at the courtroom, the animals and the dust. And then, real quiet, he says he's seen what's best for a man.

cards.question: What does the Teacher say there's nothing better for a man than?
The Teacher says enjoying his work is a man's lot. What does he say nobody can bring a man to see?

cards.text: Then the Teacher looks again, and this time he considers all the oppression taking place under the sun. He sees the tears of the oppressed.

cards.question: The oppressed are in tears. What does the Teacher say they don't have?
The Teacher sees that the ___ lay in the hands of their oppressors.

cards.text: And there it is again: no comforter. So the Teacher weighs the dead against the living.

cards.question: The Teacher says he admired the living above the dead.

cards.text: I've had some dark years under the takeout menus in a junk drawer, friend, and even I need a minute with that one. But the Teacher's not done, because he names someone better off than both.

cards.question: Who does the Teacher say is better off than both the dead and the living?

answers.text: Someone who has not yet existed

cards.question: That one is better off because he hasn't seen the ___ that is done under the sun.

findings.problem: The opening card says 'He just said there's a time for everything,' which gives away the answer to the card 5 blank ('there is a ___ for every activity and every deed' → time). It also says 'God will call to account what has passed,' which comes close to giving away card 4 (God will judge the righteous and the wicked).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: 'So the Teacher says something in his heart about God' adds a cause-and-effect link between 3:16 and 3:17. Verse 17 just begins 'I said in my heart' and never says he said it because of what he saw.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The question opens with 'God will judge them.' The word 'them' points back to card 4, which is no longer on screen. The question should name the righteous and the wicked.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The story card is a flat restatement of 3:21 with none of Papa Dorin's voice: 'Then the Teacher brings up the spirit of man rising upward and the spirit of the animal going down into the earth.'

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The card calls the 'place of judgment' (3:16) 'the courtroom.' The text never uses that word.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The first sentence, 'He's looked at the courtroom, the animals and the dust,' recaps earlier cards instead of moving the passage forward.
'The ___ lay in the hands of their oppressors' does not say whose oppressors. 'Their' points back to the oppressed from earlier cards, which are no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'That one is better off' points back to the answer on card 7, which is no longer on screen. The question should say who is meant: the one who has not yet existed.
